piątek, 16 października 2026 21:20, Hal — HeliumDeploy Support <(email hidden)> napisał(a):
Searched the web · Bitaxe Gamma "power fault" AxeOS ESP-Miner input voltage thr
Searched the web · ESP-Miner POWER_FAULT "Power fault" github bitaxe voltage be
Searched the web · ESP-Miner source "power fault" input voltage threshold 4.8V

Hello,

Thanks, that reading tells me exactly what the miner is complaining about. The "Power fault detected, mining not available" message comes from AxeOS itself, not from a broken chip: the firmware watches the 5V input and the TPS546 regulator on the board, and if that rail sits outside its window it refuses to start the ASIC and shows that line. At 4.7V under load the firmware is doing its job. Nothing on the board is damaged, and the Gamma will not start hashing until it sees roughly 5.0V or more at the board.

The M. Well LRS-50-5 that comes with the unit leaves the factory trimmed to the low side of its range, and with the Gamma pulling its full current the rail sags to the 4.7V you measured. That supply has a small adjustment screw for exactly this, a potentiometer marked SVR or +V ADJ on the end of the metal case next to the DC output terminals. You do not need to open anything. Unplug the supply from the wall, turn that screw clockwise about an eighth of a turn with a small flat screwdriver, plug it back in, let the miner boot, and read the input voltage on the AxeOS dashboard in your browser. Repeat in small steps until it reads between 5.0V and 5.1V while the miner is running, and stop there. Do not go past 5.2V, do not take the metal cover off, and keep the screwdriver well away from the AC terminal block marked L, N and earth; only adjust with the mains lead out of the socket.

If the fault message is still there once the rail reads 5.0V or above, there is a second, well documented cause with the same wording. When a Gamma overheats, the firmware throttles it by dropping the ASIC core voltage, and on some versions it could save a value below 1000mV, which is under the minimum the TPS546 regulator will accept. The regulator then never comes up cleanly, the power fault sticks, and it survives reboots and even a new power supply. The cure is in AxeOS under Settings: set the core voltage back to the stock value for the Gamma (anything at or above 1150mV is safe, the default) and the frequency back to stock as well, then save and restart. People have chased this for days and swapped supplies for nothing, when the fault clears the instant the voltage goes back above 1000mV.

Last step, update AxeOS to the current release from the firmware page in the web UI. The fix that stops the throttle writing that invalid voltage was merged in September 2026, so a unit on older firmware can fall back into the same state after a hot day.

If it still shows the power fault after all three, send me the voltage AxeOS reports, your AxeOS version number and what the screen shows, and I will take it from there. The fastest second opinion in the meantime is our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , where you can tag @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead).

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
